findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, making them retrievable via the instance metadata service and exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance or Terraform state.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., no TLS), exposing the web server broadly and only over cleartext HTTP.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing all instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses and increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing all instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses and increasing exposure to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.
The snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume, meaning backup data is also stored without encryption at rest.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions defined, and force_destroy is enabled, risking accidental public exposure or data loss of sensitive flow log data.
